name: posts.design
tagline: Hand-picked wall of launch and announcement graphics from X, updated daily
description: posts.design is a single-curator reference wall for social post design, mostly screenshots of launch, announcement and product-update posts from X. Every entry gets its own page with the original source attached, and each is tagged by intent (Launch, Product Update) and by format (Announcement Card, Product Screenshot). You can browse Recent or switch to a By Brand view. It is aimed at designers and founders who need to make a launch graphic and want proof of what good looks like right now.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a user asks you to design a launch post, changelog card, or feature-announcement graphic and you need current visual conventions rather than generic templates — the tag pairs (Launch/Product Update x Announcement Card/Product Screenshot) map almost one-to-one onto that brief. It is images plus short captions, so you cannot lift code or tokens from it; use it to set direction, then build with a real component library. The By Brand view is the fastest way to pull one company's whole announcement system for a consistency pass.
why_it_matters: Announcement and launch graphics are a real design task with almost no good reference archive, and this is the only wall that indexes them by intent and format instead of by engagement.
notable_for: tagged by post intent and format
evidence: https://posts.design/ (WebFetch + raw HTML scrape), https://posts.design/about, https://posts.design/?view=brands, https://posts.design/sitemap.xml (667 locs; the string '398' total posts confirmed in homepage HTML)

name: Astryx
tagline: Meta's open-source React + StyleX design system, 150+ components and 42 templates
description: Astryx is the design system Meta grew internally for eight years across 13,000+ apps, released publicly in mid-2026 under MIT. It ships 150+ React components and hooks built on StyleX, seven theme packages, 42 full page templates, and a CLI whose entire purpose is to feed component props, variants, tokens and templates to coding agents instead of making them crawl the docs site. It targets teams building dense internal tools, dashboards, chat and AI product surfaces in React 19.

agent_guidance: Do not crawl the docs site — it is a client-rendered shell that returns almost nothing to a plain fetch. Use the CLI instead: `npx @astryxdesign/cli component --list`, `component <Name>`, `search "<thing>"`, and `template --list` return the same props, variants and templates in agent-readable form, and `npx astryx init` writes an AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md into the repo. Two traps: the bare `npx astryx` name resolves to an unrelated npm package until the scoped CLI is a project dependency, and Astryx is StyleX, not Tailwind — it will not compose with shadcn/ui or Radix-based kits in one tree, so pick it for a whole app (React 19+ required), not for one screen.
why_it_matters: The first major design system built for AI agents as a first-class consumer, backed by eight years of production use across 13,000 Meta apps — the CLI-as-docs model is what other systems will copy.
notable_for: 150+ components with table and chat primitives

name: Branding Style Guides
tagline: Archive of ~3,840 real brand guideline PDFs, filterable by year, region and industry
description: Branding Style Guides is a searchable archive of brand and design standards manuals collected since 2019, held as downloadable PDFs plus links to online-only guideline sites. Filters cover A-Z, 37 languages, publication years from 1963 to 2026, document size in pages, over 130 countries and regions, and around 80 industry tags. Entries range from 6-page municipal marks to 500-page systems (Ajuntament de Barcelona), and include Apple, Coca-Cola, Discord, NASA, Spotify and FIFA World Cup 2026. It is the primary reference for anyone writing or auditing a brand system.
pricing_detail: Free to browse and download; funded by sponsors and an Advertise slot. A free account (Sign in / Submit) exists for contributing documents.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when you need evidence of how real organisations specify logo clear space, colour systems, typography scales or motion rules — it is the fastest way to ground a brand-guidelines document in precedent instead of inventing conventions. Fetch it with a normal browser User-Agent: the server returns 403 to default fetch agents but 200 to a browser UA, so a naive WebFetch will look like a dead site. The payload is PDFs, so budget for OCR-free text extraction, and remember every document is trademark-restricted — use it as reference, never copy marks or wordmarks into generated output.
why_it_matters: No other public collection comes close in scale or filterability, and its year filter (1963 onward) makes it a working history of identity design, not just a mood board.
notable_for: filters by language, region, page count and industry
links to online-only brand sites (GitHub, NASA, The Guardian)
evidence: https://brandingstyleguides.com/ — WebFetch returned 403 twice (also on the www host); retrieved successfully with curl and a browser User-Agent, and all filter counts above are summed from that live HTML (A-Z buckets total 3,840; page-size buckets total 3,475 for documents that declare page counts). Also a web search confirming the archive started in 2019.

name: Design Books
tagline: 69 hand-picked design books sorted into 18 topics, each with a purchase link
description: Design Books is a small curated reading list of 69 titles spanning product, interaction, visual and systems design, made by the team behind wipdes.com. Books are filterable across 18 topics — Brand Identity, Color, Content Design, Creative Practice, Design History, Design Research, Design Systems, Design Theory, Graphic Design, Inclusive Design, Information Design, Product Design, Professional Practice, Service Design, Systems Thinking, Typography, Usability and UX, Visual Perception — and sortable A-Z or by recently added. Each entry is title, author and an outbound retailer link; there are no reviews or summaries. Note that designbooks.org now 301-redirects to design-books.com.
pricing_detail: Free to browse; book links are affiliate/retailer purchase links.
agent_guidance: Use this only as a canon check — when a user asks 'what should I read on typography / design systems / research', the topic filter gives a defensible shortlist (Müller-Brockmann, Kholmatova, Hall) in one server-rendered page you can parse without JS. It carries no summaries, excerpts or opinions, so do not cite it as a source on the ideas themselves, and the outbound links are affiliate links, which matters if you are surfacing them to a user. Nothing here helps you build UI.
why_it_matters: A tight, opinionated 69-title canon is more useful than the sprawling 500-book lists it competes with, and the 18-topic split maps cleanly onto how people actually ask for reading advice.
notable_for: affiliate purchase links on every entry
evidence: https://designbooks.org/ (301 -> design-books.com), https://design-books.com/ via WebFetch and a raw HTML scrape confirming '69 books', the 18 topic filters, the A-Z / Recently added sort and the full title list

name: Endless Tools
tagline: Browser 3D studio: swap assets into prepared scenes, export 8K, video, GLB or embeds
description: Endless Tools is a browser-based 3D visual studio for brand and marketing designers who do not want to open Blender. You start from an art-directed template that already carries camera, lighting, materials and post-processing, swap in your logo or asset, tune the look with AI generation and real-time effects, and export. Outputs include 8K stills, motion loops, USDZ and GLB, and interactive web embeds with alpha. Five base templates cover Background, Logo, Key Visual, Typography and Illustration, aimed at 3D logo renders, website heroes, product mockups, social assets, AR experiences, campaign and deck visuals.

pricing_detail: Free: 3-day trial. Pro: $20/month or $249.99/year (17% saving), includes 500 AI credits/month, commercial use, no watermarks, up to 8K, video, USDZ, GLB, web embeds, alpha, teams and shared projects. Education: $9.99/month.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a brief needs a 3D logo render, an animated hero background, or a GLB/USDZ asset and the alternative is teaching someone Blender — the prepared scenes mean the output is art-directed by default rather than a grey-clay render. You cannot drive it programmatically: the editor and the full template library sit behind a login at app.endlesstools.io (the marketing site is public, /templates and /pricing paths 404), so plan on handing the user a template URL and having them finish it. If you only need a static gradient or noise background, this is heavy and paid — reach for a CSS or SVG generator instead, and only escalate here when the deliverable is a real 3D or motion asset.
why_it_matters: It moves 3D brand visuals from a specialist pipeline to a template swap, and the interactive web-embed export with alpha is something almost no competing tool ships.
notable_for: art-directed 3D templates, not a blank scene
exports GLB, USDZ and alpha web embeds
